A/ Find training and test set AUC for a built - from - scratch CNN model:

1. Delete folder ‘cell_images/cell_images’:

############## Turn to comments from the second run onwards ###############
# unlink('cell_images/cell_images', recursive = TRUE)

Unlike some preprocessing steps in tabular data (like normalization / standardization, filling in missing values, …), format conversion and resizing do not involve calculations and transformations based on data distributions that may affect the learning process of the model. These two steps are just used to ensure consistent input format and size for the model to work properly on the dataset. Therefore, instead of:

  • Checking for any inconsistencies in the format of the images based on just the training set, then based on the result, convert all images from the training, validation and test set to the same format,

  • As well as finding the range of image height and width from just the training set, then based on the result, resize all images to the same size,

We can:

  • Check for any inconsistencies in the format of the images based on the whole dataset, then based on the result, convert all images from the training, validation and test set to the same format,

  • As well as finding the range of image height and width from the whole dataset, then based on the result, resize all images to the same size.

For this approach, we only need to apply resizing and format conversion steps once at the begining then save the processed images for future code runs, instead of having to re - run these steps every time we split the train - validation - test set differently. This is practical and helps simplify the coding process.

5. Get the list of images and the list of labels:

# Get the list of image paths and the list of categorical labels 
image_paths <- list()
labels <- list()
for (class_folder in class_folders) {
  images <- list.files(file.path(main_folder, class_folder), full.names = TRUE, pattern = "\\.png$")
  image_paths <- c(image_paths, images)
  labels <- c(labels, rep(class_folder, length(images)))
}

# Load the images
X <- lapply(unlist(image_paths), load.image)

# Label encoding
y <- ifelse(unlist(labels) == "Parasitized", 1, 0)

6. Split training - test - validation sets:

set.seed(1)

# Shuffle X and labels in the same order to make sure the label values appear in a random order 
shuffle_indices <- sample(1:length(X))
X <- X[shuffle_indices]
y <- y[shuffle_indices]

# Split train : test : val as 70 : 20 : 10
train_indices_temp <- createDataPartition(y, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
test_indices <- setdiff(seq_along(y), train_indices_temp)
# -> seq_along(x) creates a sequence of integers with the same length as x

X_train_temp <- X[train_indices_temp]
y_train_temp <- y[train_indices_temp]
X_test <- X[test_indices]
y_test <- y[test_indices]

val_indices <- createDataPartition(y_train_temp, p = 0.125, list = FALSE)
train_indices <- setdiff(seq_along(y_train_temp), val_indices)

X_train <- X_train_temp[train_indices]
y_train <- y_train_temp[train_indices]
X_val <- X_train_temp[val_indices]
y_val <- y_train_temp[val_indices]
# (train: 0.875 x 0.8 = 0.7 ; val: 0.125 x 0.8 = 0.1)

# Examine the size of the training, validation, and test sets
cat("Train set's size: X_train = ", length(X_train), ", y_train = ", length(y_train), "\n")
## Train set's size: X_train =  19292 , y_train =  19292
cat("Validation set's size: X_val = ", length(X_val), ", y_val = ", length(y_val), "\n")
## Validation set's size: X_val =  2756 , y_val =  2756
cat("Test set's size: X_test = ", length(X_test), ", y_test = ", length(y_test), "\n")
## Test set's size: X_test =  5510 , y_test =  5510
# Check the pixel value range of training images
cat("Pixel value range of training images: [", min(unlist(X_train)), ",", max(unlist(X_train)), "] \n")
## Pixel value range of training images: [ 0 , 1 ]
# -> All training images are already normalized

8. Apply other preprocessing steps and show some image samples:

All training images are already normalized, so there is no need to normalize the training, validation and test set.

# # One - hot encode the labels (not needed when using sigmoid activation function in last FC layer in binary classification)
# y_train_ <- keras::to_categorical(y_train)
# y_val_ <- keras::to_categorical(y_val)
# y_test_ <- keras::to_categorical(y_test)

# Reshape the images
xtr <- do.call(rbind, X_train)
X_train_ <- array_reshape(xtr, c(dim(xtr)[1], 50, 50, 3), order = "F")
xv <- do.call(rbind, X_val)
X_val_ <- array_reshape(xv, c(dim(xv)[1], 50, 50, 3), order = "F")
xte <- do.call(rbind, X_test)
X_test_ <- array_reshape(xte, c(dim(xte)[1], 50, 50, 3), order = "F")
# order = "C" means elements should be read in row-major order, with the last index changing fastest; "F" means elements should be read in column-major order, with the first index changing fastest.

# Show some samples in the dataset
labels_tr <- c()
labels_te <- c()
labels_tr <- ifelse(y_train == 1, "Parasitized", "Uninfected")
labels_te <- ifelse(y_test == 1, "Parasitized", "Uninfected")

# Display the 1080th image from the training set

9. Build the CNN model:

# Initialize the Sequential model
my_model <- keras_model_sequential()

# Block 1
my_model %>%
  layer_conv_2d(filters = 16, input_shape = c(50, 50, 3), kernel_size = c(3, 3), strides = c(1, 1), padding = 'same', name = 'Block_1_Conv_1') %>%
  layer_batch_normalization() %>%
  layer_activation('relu') %>%
  layer_conv_2d(filters = 32, kernel_size = c(3, 3), strides = c(1, 1), padding = 'same', name = 'Block_1_Conv_2') %>%
  layer_batch_normalization() %>%
  layer_activation('relu') %>%
  layer_max_pooling_2d(pool_size = c(2, 2), strides = c(2, 2), padding = 'same', name = 'Block_1_MaxPool') %>%
  layer_dropout(rate = 0.2)

# Block 2
my_model %>%
  layer_conv_2d(filters = 64, kernel_size = c(3, 3), strides = c(1, 1), padding = 'same', name = 'Block_2_Conv_1') %>%
  layer_batch_normalization() %>%
  layer_activation('relu') %>%
  layer_conv_2d(filters = 128, kernel_size = c(3, 3), strides = c(1, 1), padding = 'same', name = 'Block_2_Conv_2') %>%
  layer_batch_normalization() %>%
  layer_activation('relu') %>%
  layer_max_pooling_2d(pool_size = c(2, 2), strides = c(2, 2), padding = 'same', name = 'Block_2_MaxPool') %>%
  layer_dropout(rate = 0.2)

# Block 3
my_model %>%
  layer_conv_2d(filters = 256, kernel_size = c(3, 3), strides = c(1, 1), padding = 'same', name = 'Block_3_Conv_1') %>%
  layer_batch_normalization() %>%
  layer_activation('relu') %>%
  layer_conv_2d(filters = 512, kernel_size = c(3, 3), strides = c(1, 1), padding = 'same', name = 'Block_3_Conv_2') %>%
  layer_batch_normalization() %>%
  layer_activation('relu') %>%
  layer_max_pooling_2d(pool_size = c(2, 2), strides = c(2, 2), padding = 'same', name = 'Block_3_MaxPool') %>%
  layer_dropout(rate = 0.2)

# Flatten
my_model %>%
  layer_flatten()

# Fully connected (FC) layer 1
my_model %>%
  layer_dense(units = 128) %>%
  layer_batch_normalization() %>%
  layer_activation('relu') %>%
  layer_dropout(rate = 0.4)

# Fully connected (FC) layer 2
my_model %>%
  layer_dense(units = 100) %>%
  layer_batch_normalization() %>%
  layer_activation('relu') %>%
  layer_dropout(rate = 0.4)

# Fully connected (FC) layer 3
my_model %>%
  layer_dense(units = 1) %>%
  layer_activation('sigmoid')

# Model Summary
summary(my_model)

10. Compile the model:

my_model %>%
  compile(loss = 'binary_crossentropy', optimizer = optimizer_sgd(learning_rate = 0.007, momentum = 0.9), metrics = list('AUC'))

11. Train the model:

############## Turn to comments from the second run onwards ###############
# Create a callback ModelCheckpoint. This callback will save the model weights when finding one better than the current best
checkpoint_filepath <- "malaria_best_model_weights.h5"
mc <- callback_model_checkpoint(filepath = checkpoint_filepath, monitor = "val_loss", save_best_only = TRUE, save_weights_only = TRUE, save_freq = "epoch", verbose = 0)

# Train the model
history <- my_model %>%
  fit(X_train_, y_train, batch_size = 32, epochs = 20, verbose = 1, validation_data = list(X_val_, y_val), callbacks = list(mc))

B/ Choosing decision threshold by ROC curve and decision curve:

1. Criterias to determine the decision threshold for the CNN model:

  • Youden index criterion:
# Optimal threshold obtained by maximizing youden index
j_threshold <- function(y_true, y_pred) {
  roc_obj <- pROC::roc(y_true, y_pred)
  fpr <- 1 - roc_obj$specificities
  tpr <- roc_obj$sensitivities
  thresholds <- roc_obj$thresholds
  j <- tpr - fpr 
  j <- sort(j, decreasing = TRUE, index.return = TRUE)
  j_ordered <- data.frame(j = j[1], thresholds = thresholds[rank(j$ix)])
  for (k in 1:nrow(j_ordered)){
    if (is.finite(j_ordered$thresholds[k])) {
      return(j_ordered$thresholds[k])
      break
      }
  }
}

cj <- j_threshold(y_test, y_test_pred)
## Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
## Setting direction: controls < cases
cj
## [1] 0.3763034
  • Closest to (0,1) criterion:
# Optimal threshold obtained by maximizing sensitivity and specificity to the extent that both are closest to 100% 
d_threshold <- function(y_true, y_pred) {
  roc_obj <- pROC::roc(y_true, y_pred)
  fpr <- 1 - roc_obj$specificities
  tpr <- roc_obj$sensitivities
  thresholds <- roc_obj$thresholds
  d <- sapply(1:length(fpr), function(i) sqrt((1 - tpr[i])^2 + (fpr[i])^2))
  d <- sort(d, decreasing = FALSE, index.return = TRUE)
  d_ordered <- data.frame(d = d[1], thresholds = thresholds[rank(d$ix)])
  for (k in 1:nrow(d_ordered)){
    if (is.finite(d_ordered$thresholds[k])) {
      return(d_ordered$thresholds[k])
      break
      }
  }
}

cd <- d_threshold(y_test, y_test_pred)
## Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
## Setting direction: controls < cases
cd
## [1] 0.2996681
  • Symetric point criterion:
# Optimal threshold obtained by finding the point where sensitivity and specificity are equivalent
s_threshold <- function(y_true, y_pred) {
  roc_obj <- pROC::roc(y_true, y_pred)
  fpr <- 1 - roc_obj$specificities
  tpr <- roc_obj$sensitivities
  thresholds <- roc_obj$thresholds
  s <- abs(fpr + tpr - 1)
  s <- sort(s, decreasing = FALSE, index.return = TRUE)
  s_ordered <- data.frame(s = s[1], thresholds = thresholds[rank(s$ix)])
  for (k in 1:nrow(s_ordered)){
    if (is.finite(s_ordered$thresholds[k])) {
      return(s_ordered$thresholds[k])
      break
      }
  }
}

cs <- s_threshold(y_test, y_test_pred)
## Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
## Setting direction: controls < cases
cs
## [1] 0.2412464

# Plot ROC curve:
roc_obj <- pROC::roc(y_test, y_test_pred)
## Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
## Setting direction: controls < cases
thresholds_cnn <- roc_obj$thresholds 
roc_data <- data.frame(fpr = rev(1 - roc_obj$specificities), tpr = rev(roc_obj$sensitivities))


for (i in 1:length(roc_obj$thresholds)){
  if (roc_obj$thresholds[i] == cj){
    specificity_j <- roc_obj$specificities[i]
    sensitivity_j <- roc_obj$sensitivities[i]
  }
  if (roc_obj$thresholds[i] == cd){
    specificity_d <- roc_obj$specificities[i]
    sensitivity_d <- roc_obj$sensitivities[i]
  }
  if (roc_obj$thresholds[i] == cs){
    specificity_s <- roc_obj$specificities[i]
    sensitivity_s <- roc_obj$sensitivities[i]
  }
}

diagonal_data <- data.frame(x = seq(0, 1, length.out = 100), y = 1 - seq(0, 1, length.out = 100))
thresholds_data <- data.frame(x1 = 0, x2 = 1 - specificity_d, y1 = 1, y2 = sensitivity_d)
sp_se_j <- data.frame(sp = specificity_j, se = sensitivity_j)
sp_se_d <- data.frame(sp = specificity_d, se = sensitivity_d)
sp_se_s <- data.frame(sp = specificity_s, se = sensitivity_s)

ggplot(data = roc_data, aes(x = fpr, y = tpr)) +
  geom_line(linetype = "solid", linewidth = 1, col = "blue") +
  geom_line(data = diagonal_data, aes(x = x, y = y), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1, col = "orange") +
  geom_segment(data = thresholds_data, aes(x = x1, y = y1, xend = x2, yend = y2), linetype = "dotdash", linewidth = 1, col = "pink") +
  geom_point(data = sp_se_j, aes(x = 1 - sp, y = se, col = "c_j"), size = 4, show.legend = TRUE) +
  geom_point(data = sp_se_d, aes(x = 1 - sp, y = se, col = "c_d"), size = 4, show.legend = TRUE) +
  geom_point(data = sp_se_s, aes(x = 1 - sp, y = se, col = "c_s"), size = 4, show.legend = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "ROC curve", x = "False positive rate", y = "True positive rate") + 
  scale_color_manual(name = "Threshold", labels = unname(TeX(c("At $\\hat{c}_{J}$", "At $\\hat{c}_{D}$", "At $\\hat{c}_{S}$"))), values=c("red", "purple", "green")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face="bold", hjust = 0.5)) 

# Plot decision curve

# Net benefit function 
nb <- function(y_true, y_pred, c, prev){
  roc_obj <- pROC::roc(y_true, y_pred)
  for (i in 1:length(roc_obj$thresholds)){
    if (roc_obj$thresholds[i] == c){
      se_c <- roc_obj$sensitivities[i]
      sp_c <- roc_obj$specificities[i]
      break
    }
  }
  phi_c <- se_c * prev - (1 - sp_c) * (1 - prev) * c/(1 - c) 
  return(phi_c)
}

# Calculate disease prevalence in the population:
p = sum(y_test)/length(y_test)
  
df_cnn <- data.frame(y_test_pred, y_test)
nb_j <- data.frame(cj = cj, nbj = nb(y_test, y_test_pred, cj, p))
## Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
## Setting direction: controls < cases
nb_d <- data.frame(cd = cd, nbd = nb(y_test, y_test_pred, cd, p))
## Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
## Setting direction: controls < cases
nb_s <- data.frame(cs = cs, nbs = nb(y_test, y_test_pred, cs, p))
## Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
## Setting direction: controls < cases
# For the Decision curve plot, use the thresholds values from ROC curve plot to make sure that the optimal thresholds show on the decision curve correctly
dcurves::dca(y_test ~ y_test_pred, data = df_cnn, label = list(y_test_pred = "CNN model"), thresholds = thresholds_cnn, prevalence = p) %>% 
  plot(smooth = FALSE) + geom_line(linewidth = 1) + labs(title = "Decision curve") +
  geom_point(data = nb_j, aes(x = cj, y = nbj, col = "c_j"), size = 4, show.legend = TRUE) +
  geom_point(data = nb_d, aes(x = cd, y = nbd, col = "c_d"), size = 4, show.legend = TRUE) +
  geom_point(data = nb_s, aes(x = cs, y = nbs, col = "c_s"), size = 4, show.legend = TRUE) + 
  scale_color_manual(labels = unname(TeX(c("Treat All", "Treat None", "CNN model", "At $\\hat{c}_{J}$", "At $\\hat{c}_{D}$", "At $\\hat{c}_{S}$"))), values=c("orange", "pink", "blue", "red", "purple", "green")) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linetype = c("solid", "solid", "solid", rep("blank", 3)), shape = c(NA, NA, NA, rep(16, 3))))) + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face="bold", hjust = 0.5))
## Assuming '1' is [Event] and '0' is [non-Event]

# Finding the optimal threshold
nb_j <- nb(y_test, y_test_pred, cj, p)
## Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
## Setting direction: controls < cases
nb_d <- nb(y_test, y_test_pred, cd, p)
## Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
## Setting direction: controls < cases
nb_s <- nb(y_test, y_test_pred, cs, p)
## Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
## Setting direction: controls < cases
nb_values <- c(cj = nb_j, cd = nb_d, cs = nb_s)

best_threshold <- names(which.max(nb_values))   # Name of the threshold with highest net benefit
threshold_map <- list(cj = cj, cd = cd, cs = cs)
c_res <- threshold_map[[best_threshold]]   # Get the optimal threshold's value 
cat("Optimal threshold:", best_threshold, "=", c_res)
## Optimal threshold: cs = 0.2412464
## Example: Predicting the class of a new data point with CNN model
new_obs_ <- X_test[2:7]  # Some observations from the test set 
new_obs <- do.call(rbind, new_obs_)
new_obs <- array_reshape(new_obs, c(dim(new_obs)[1], 50, 50, 3), order = "F")  
# In the procedure: You need to preprocess (Convert into the correct format, Resize, Normalize, Reshape, ... in the same method and with the same values calculated from the preprocessing step of the training set) the new data if needed 
actual_classes <- y_test[2:7]
class_preds <- c()

y_pred <- predict(my_model, new_obs, verbose = 0)  
y_pred = round(y_pred, digits = 7)
class_preds <- ifelse(y_pred >= c_res, "Parasitized", "Uninfected")   
actual_classes <- ifelse(actual_classes == 1, "Parasitized", "Uninfected")

# Final result 
par(mfrow = c(3, 2))  # Create subplots with 2 rows and 3 columns 

for (i in 1:nrow(new_obs)){
  suppressWarnings(plot(as.cimg(new_obs[i,,,])))
  title(main = paste0("Observation ", i, "\n Predicted class: ", class_preds[i], "; Actual class: ", actual_classes[i]), sub = paste0("Predicted probability: ", y_pred[i]), cex.main = 1.4, cex.sub = 1.4)
}
